question.question:
Use exact arithmetic. A merger yields run-rate pre-tax cost savings of 42.5 USD million per year, realized 40 percent in year 1, 85 percent in year 2 and fully from year 3 onward. Integration costs are 45 USD million in year 1 and 1.5 USD million in year 2, none later. Tax rate is 21 percent. Each year's after-tax net cash flow equals realized savings minus integration cost, times one minus the tax-rate ratio; a negative pre-tax net gets a tax credit at the same rate. Cumulative net cash starts at zero and accrues evenly within each year. Break-even time is 0 if year-1 net cash flow is non-negative; otherwise, if the cumulative balance first reaches zero or more during year k, it equals k minus 1 plus the shortfall at the start of year k divided by year k's net cash flow. Find break-even time in years.

Answer format: use exact arithmetic through all intermediate steps, round only the final value half up to 4 decimal digits, and return only the numeric value interpreted in `years` with no unit label or additional text.

slots.description: After-tax net cash flow in year 1, negative if a net cost.
Cumulative after-tax net cash at the end of year 2.
Year in which cumulative balance first reaches zero or more.
